ACCEPT. Under the prior results you explicitly grant, the perpendicular-source classification, coalesced parallel-tip count, crossing corrections, and exact initial ledger are sound. The construction is feasible for every even  $W\ge22$  and establishes the claimed failure of the unchanged local rule  $D_G\ge2B$ .I find no mathematical gap or counterexample to the proposed crossing-loss theorem. There is one wording clarification worth making: the coefficient-one conclusion applies to the subclass satisfying  $K+O\le B+J$ , or another condition that makes the exact ledger nonnegative. Section 1’s coverage hypotheses alone give the crossing-loss bound (8).1. Perpendicular sources: the two cases are exhaustiveThe prescribed alignment is essential and is used correctly. After a tile-preserving change of coordinates, a rightward source can be written as
$$P_K=
\bigl(\{1,\ldots,w\}\times\{0,1\}\bigr)
\;\cup\;
\bigl(\{1,w\}\times\{2,\ldots,r\}\bigr),
\qquad r=2h+2.$$
Physical tiles start at even rows and even columns. The chamber therefore occupies one physical column pair, starts on an odd row, and ends on an even row.Consequently, a physical row band meeting its endpoints is either:an interior band containing two chamber rows; orone of the two end bands, containing one chamber end row and its exterior neighbor.There is no additional partially intersected chamber case.The forced-blank strip extremes also justify containment. In an end band, the endpoints form a consecutive horizontal path. If some but not all of that path lay in the strip, the path would pass through a forced-blank extreme column. Thus a strip meeting the path contains it completely.Interior chamber bandThe physical endpoint square has four endpoints and no selections, so its raw excess is zero.The shifted partition produces two endpoint squares, each with a column of two endpoints. The other column contains no additional endpoints, by the prescribed complete component and the granted ownership property. It contains at most one selected vertex: two selections there would be adjacent to each other, and each would also be adjacent to an endpoint.Thus, with  $a,b\in\{0,1\}$ ,
$$E_i(K)=0,\qquad
E'_i(K)=(-1+a)+(-1+b),$$
and
$$E_i(K)-E'_i(K)=2-a-b\ge0.$$
In particular, both flank selections can eliminate the entire gain. Your proof correctly allows this and does not assume a gain of two.End-row arm bandThe endpoint path has  $r+1$  vertices, an odd number. In the physical partition, its full endpoint tiles have  $(p,t)=(2,1)$ , and its terminal tile has  $(p,t)=(1,2)$ . Therefore
$$E_i(K)=\frac12.$$
In the shifted partition, all full endpoint tiles still have  $(p,t)=(2,1)$ . The chamber-side singleton square contains one endpoint and the required lateral support. The corner diagonally opposite the endpoint is forced blank: occupying it would give that selected support a second occupied neighbor. The remaining corner may be selected or blank, and cannot contain another endpoint.Writing its optional selection as  $a\in\{0,1\}$ ,
$$E'_i(K)=-\frac12+a,
\qquad
E_i(K)-E'_i(K)=1-a\ge0.$$
The terminal axial support now lies in a shifted square without endpoints. Its contribution belongs in  $D'_i$ , exactly as your accounting requires.The resulting table is therefore:
$$\begin{array}{c|c|c|c}
\text{Band type}&E_i(K)&E'_i(K)&E_i(K)-E'_i(K)\\ \hline
\text{Interior chamber}&0&a+b-2&2-a-b\\
\text{End-row arm}&\tfrac12&a-\tfrac12&1-a
\end{array}$$
Tile-preserving reflections preserve both the physical and shifted pairings, so they introduce no further phase case. Optional selections need not be independently realizable; the argument only uses their actual values in the given feasible configuration.Thus the new assertion  $A_i\ge0$ , with integer gains, is proved.2. Coalescing and the parallel-tip identityThe interval argument for
$$\sum_iL_i=2B-2C$$
is correct, including when perpendicular contacts occur.Represent a mouth in a fixed physical row band by its physical-tile interval  $[a,b]$ . Its terminal tip tiles are immediately outside that interval, at  $a-1$  and  $b+1$ .For a coalesced strip containing  $b_i$  member mouths:precisely the leftmost and rightmost terminal tip tiles lie outside the union;every other member tip tile lies inside;distinct tips cannot occupy the same physical tile, by the granted endpoint-component ownership and the prescribed source geometry.There is also no uncounted tip from a nonmember parallel source. If such a tip lay in the strip, its adjacent mouth would overlap or be adjacent to the strip, forcing coalescence.Therefore
$$L_i=2b_i-2,$$
and summing gives
$$\sum_iL_i=2\sum_i b_i-2C=2B-2C.$$
A perpendicular strip may contain one of the excluded extreme tips, but that tip is not parallel to that strip and hence does not contribute to its  $L_i$ . This is precisely why perpendicular intersections do not alter the identity.Coalescing introduces no new tiles beyond the union of the overlapping or adjacent mouth intervals, so it also preserves the stated mouth-endpoint coverage.3. Strip identity and crossing signsThe raw strip calculation is exact. Removing the two forced-blank extreme columns preserves the occupied weight  $\mu_i$ , while reducing the number of squares from  $n_i$  to  $n_i-1$ . Hence
$$D_i-D'_i
=
2+\sum_K\bigl(E_i(K)-E'_i(K)\bigr),$$
which gives
$$D_i=2+L_i+U_i-S_i+A_i+D'_i.$$
Every no-endpoint square contains at most two selected vertices. Indeed, three vertices of a unit square contain a selected vertex adjacent to two selected vertices. Thus  $D'_i\ge0$ .For the crossing correction, it helps to introduce three explicit quantities: $D_\times$ : the sum of deficits of no-endpoint crossing tiles; $s_\times$ : the number of sparse comb-end crossing tiles; $u_\times$ : the number of saturated comb-end crossing tiles.Then
$$\sum_iD_i=D_G+D_\times.$$
For the comb ends,
$$\sum_i(U_i-S_i)=J-O+u_\times-s_\times.$$
Here  $J-O$  is correct even for a comb with both end flags: its two union memberships cancel.Summing the strip identities and using the tip identity yields
$$D_G+D_\times
=
2B+J-O+u_\times-s_\times+A+\sum_iD'_i.$$
Consequently,
$$D_G
=
2B+J-O
-\underbrace{(D_\times+s_\times-u_\times)}_{K}
+A+\sum_iD'_i.$$
This verifies every sign in your crossing table:Crossing typeContribution to  $K$ ReasonNo endpoint $2-t_Q$ Remove the duplicated physical deficitSparse comb end $+1$ Correct the duplicated negative end contributionSaturated comb end $-1$ Correct the duplicated positive end contributionOther endpoint tile $0$ No physical no-endpoint deficit or comb-end multiplicity to correctIn particular, the negative sign for a saturated comb-end crossing is correct.Each contribution lies between  $-1$  and  $2$ , giving
$$-X\le K\le2X.$$
A crossing tile containing source endpoints requires no additional physical-donor correction. Its phase contributions have already entered the strip identities through  $L_i$  or  $A_i$ . The derivation does not treat shifted squares as a second collection of physical resources.4. The exact initial ledger followsLet  $\rho(F)\le0$  denote the corrected charge of a final nonprescribed receiver. Your remainder can be written explicitly as
$$R=
D_{\mathrm{outside}\,G}
+\sum_{F\text{ nonprescribed}}(-\rho(F))
\ge0.$$
The whole-component ledger then gives
$$\frac{mn}{2}-|T|-|M|
=
D_G-B+R,$$
because the prescribed sources contribute  $+B$  and the complete combs contribute zero.Objective-preserving normalization replaces  $|T|+|M|$  by  $|T_0|+|M_0|$ . Substitution of the union identity gives exactly
$$\frac{mn}{2}-|T_0|-|M_0|
=
B+J-O-K+A+\sum_iD'_i+R.$$
Discarding the nonnegative terms proves
$$|T_0|+|M_0|
\le
\frac{mn}{2}-B+O-J+K
\le
\frac{mn}{2}-B+O-J+2X.$$
Thus both the exact criterion
$$K+O\le B+J$$
and the sufficient coarse criterion
$$2X+O\le B+J$$
are valid.The crossing-pair consequence also follows: with no combs,  $B=2r$  and  $X=r$ , the coarse correction is exactly cancelled. Adding isolated sources supplies additional margin through the  $-B$  term.5. The arbitrary-width construction is validUsing your baseline convention, the coordinate map for the rightward source is
$$(x,y)\longmapsto(y+7,x+6).$$
This is the prescribed  $(2,3)$  placement, followed by transposition and translation by  $(4,4)$ . It gives exactly the chamber and tip coordinates stated for  $K$ .Feasibility and component separationThe prescribed supports of  $H$  are:rows  $2,4,6,\ldots,16$ , at columns  $2,W+3$ ;rows  $5,7,\ldots,15$ , at columns  $4,W+1$ ;row  $17$ , at columns  $3,W+2$ .There are  $30$ .The prescribed supports of  $K$  are:rows  $6,21$ , at columns  $6,8,10,12,14,16$ ;rows  $8,19$ , at columns  $9,11,13,15$ ;rows  $7,20$ , at column  $17$ .There are  $22$ .The two endpoint sets are nonadjacent. Their prescribed supports also acquire no additional occupied neighbors from the other source.For the 19 fixed additions, their occupied-neighborhood classification is exact:the six displayed selected pairs are isolated pairs; $(16,5)$  has sole occupied neighbor  $(16,6)$ ; $(16,8)$  has sole occupied neighbor  $(16,7)$ ;the five vertices
$$(11,17),(16,11),(16,14),(16,16),(17,15)$$
have no occupied neighbors.No added vertex is adjacent to a prescribed support.For every even  $18\le c\le W$ , each tail vertex at column  $c$  has exactly its vertical mate as occupied neighbor. The intervening columns are blank in the two mouth rows. At  $c=W$ , the nearby inside support is diagonal, and the arm and axial support are two columns away.These are uniform coordinate arguments for all  $W\ge22$ , rather than conclusions extrapolated from tested widths.The selected and matching counts are therefore
$$|T|=30+22+19+(W-16)=W+55,$$
and
$$|M|=(W+13)+23=W+36.$$
Physical mouth deficitsFor  $H$ , the physical mouth tiles have the following contents:ColumnsContents $4,5$ One selection $6,7$ Four  $K$ -endpoints $8,9;\ 10,11;\ 12,13;\ 14,15$ Two selections each $16,17$ One selectionEvery remaining even pair  $c,c+1$ ,  $18\le c\le W$ Two selectionsThus  $D_H=2$ .The six physical row pairs in  $K$ ’s mouth contain respectively

selected vertices and no endpoints. Thus  $D_K=2$ .The unique crossing tile contains only  $(16,16)$ , so
$$X=1,\qquad K=1,\qquad D_G=2+2-1=3.$$
Shifted deficits and phase gainFor  $H$ , the shifted endpoint squares at columns  $5,6$  and  $7,8$  each contain two endpoints and one selection. The two selections are exactly the optional flanks
$$(16,5),\qquad(16,8).$$
Hence the perpendicular phase gain is
$$2-1-1=0.$$
Every remaining shifted square has two selected vertices: this holds directly for the initial shifted pairs and uniformly along the tail. Therefore  $D'_H=0$ .For  $K$ , each shifted row pair
$$9,10;\quad11,12;\quad13,14;\quad15,16;\quad17,18$$
contains two selected vertices, giving  $D'_K=0$ . There are no source endpoints in this mouth, so it adds no perpendicular-source gain.All of (9) follows:
$$B=2,\quad X=1,\quad O=J=0,\quad K=1,\quad
D_G=3,\quad A=0,\quad \sum_iD'_i=0.$$
What the example establishesThe local union identity is attained:
$$D_G=2B-K=4-1=3.$$
Accordingly, the unchanged rule  $D_G\ge2B$  fails in the enlarged contact class.The full rectangle has substantial exterior slack. Directly,
$$\frac{28(W+10)}2-(|T|+|M|)
=
14W+140-(2W+91)
=
12W+49.$$
The corresponding exterior remainder is
$$R=12W+48,$$
and the exact initial ledger reads
$$12W+49=2-1+(12W+48).$$
This confirms your stated distinction: the construction defeats the unchanged local payment rule while still paying both source charges, and it does not refute a global strict-margin statement.6. One editorial clarificationI would replace“This removes the entire  $|M_0|/6$  loss … for this stated class”with:“For the subclass satisfying  $K+O\le B+J$ —in particular,  $2X+O\le B+J$ —this removes the entire  $|M_0|/6$  loss in the stated universal bound.”The preceding criterion already supports that reading, so this is a clarification of scope rather than a mathematical repair.The theorem and the explicit obstacle are accepted under the supplied grants.
